scope.sensitivity: sanitized engineering/provider evidence; no credentials or user content

owner_decision.directive: Auto routing remains default; exact-model manual selection is supported by the central router; Bedrock catalog uses live AWS truth; phone-local AI is optional and OFF by default.
owner_decision.probe_authorization: One bounded runtime invocation per conversational Bedrock model, smallest prompt, minimal provider-valid max tokens, one attempt each, no retry/load loops.

durable_lessons: AWS Bedrock discovery/authorization metadata is not runtime proof; Routable requires a successful bounded provider invocation plus current agreement, authorization, entitlement and region availability.

SigV4 path signing must canonicalize colon-bearing Bedrock model IDs exactly once. Carry the raw ':' in the wire URL and RFC3986-encode it in the canonical URI; pre-encoding the path causes a signature mismatch.
Provider-minimal probes should omit optional inference fields unless required. Kimi K3 rejects temperature and requires maxTokens >= 16; other current conversational probe candidates use maxTokens=1.
A catalog-only AWS sync must preserve existing runtime and cost evidence only when the invocation target is unchanged. Changed targets invalidate runtime proof; removed models retire.

Never re-probe automatically after an implementation defect when the owner authorized one attempt per model. Fix source, preserve the failed evidence, and require new spend authorization for any second invocation.
Phone-local AI must be a device preference that defaults OFF and fail-closes local prewarm, routing, generation and residency. Enabling local AI makes it an allowed candidate, not a priority.

open_loop.implication: Do not build/merge the model picker into the composer until Lane E global active-chat shell lands and Lane F UI work is rebased on current main.
open_loop.re_probe_requirement: The 22 fully available models whose first attempt was masked by the signer defect remain non-routable until a new explicit paid-probe authorization allows a second invocation.
